description:
pkix-lint/src/oscal/parse.rs::parse_risk and pkix-lint/src/oscal/parse.rs::parse_subject read multiple variable-length string fields from attacker-supplied JSON via `Value::as_str().to_string()` with no upper-length cap enforced before allocation:

- `obj.get("description").and_then(Value::as_str).ok_or(...)?.to_string()` (parse.rs:576-580) — `justification`
- `required_nonempty_prop` for `pkix-lint.deviation-id`, `pkix-lint.target-lint`, `pkix-lint.action`, `pkix-lint.authorized-by` (parse.rs:589-608) — each becomes a heap-allocated String

A malicious OSCAL Risk JSON with a 100MB `description` (justification) string allocates 100MB on parse, plus another copy through DeviationStore::add, plus another copy on every subsequent OSCAL emit of the same store. `hex_decode` (parse.rs:834-848) similarly allocates without a length cap, although DER bytes are typically bounded by certificate size anyway.

Section C (untrusted input — memory-DoS via variable-length fields). What goes wrong: availability. `deviation_store_from_risks` is the inverse of `risks_from_store` and is the documented entry point for ingesting deviation policy from operator-provided JSON. That JSON crosses a trust boundary in any deployment where the deviation file is fetched from a network source or shared filesystem.

serde_json's default 128-level recursion limit prevents stack-overflow attacks but does not bound individual string lengths.

P3 defense-in-depth, not P1:
- Operators typically curate their own deviation JSON, not adversaries
- Even if adversarial, the attack vector is "crash the audit pipeline" not "forge a deviation"

Fix shape:
- Document the expected upper bound on each field (deviation IDs <= 64 chars, justifications <= 4KB) and reject longer values with a typed ParseError variant before allocation
- Or document explicitly that callers MUST cap input size (e.g., via `serde_json::Deserializer::from_reader` with a length-limited reader) before invoking `deviation_store_from_risks`

Section C requires bounded variable-length fields at protocol boundaries; pkix-lint's OSCAL parse path is such a boundary.
notes: Duplicate of PKIX-hy2e.40 (open, P3) filed in the prior crypto-security pass on pkix-lint. hy2e.40 captures the hex_decode-specific case; this issue named description/justification/authorized-by which are not in hy2e.40 — but the underlying defense-in-depth principle (Section C explicit upper bounds on variable-length fields) is the same and the fix shape is identical (early-return checks before allocation). The hex_decode case is the most exploitable; description/justification are operator-supplied so secondary. Closing as substantive duplicate. If the maintainer wants the description/justification subset broken out separately, can reopen under a tighter title.
title: OSCAL Risk parse path accepts unbounded string lengths for description/justification/authorized-by/prop values
